newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia needs lower inflation, interest rates - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia needs lower inflation, interest rates - IMF.

text.p: Slovenia's primary monetary tasks for the next two years should be bringing down both inflation and interest rates, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday.

"Slovenia has to work in the areas of achieving lower inflation and interest rates in the future," said Hans Flickenschild, head of the IMF annual mission to Slovenia at a news conference in Ljubljana.
Slovenia's annual inflation rate rose to 10.3 percent in August from 8.6 percent at the end of 1995.
Average interbank money morket interest rates rose to 18.0 percent in June from 15.9 percent at the end of last year.
However, Flickenschild said Slovenia had already fulfilled the most difficult criteria of the Maastricht treaty by having a balanced fiscal position.
He also acknowledged Slovenia's progress in reaching agreements on the division of debt and assets of the former Yugoslavia.
"We are very heartened by the progress of settling the outstanding obligations," Flickenschild said.
Slovenia was the first of the former Yugoslav republics to reach an accord with the former Yugoslavia's commercial creditors to shoulder 18 percent of the $4.3 billion ex-Yugo debt.
In June, Slovenia completed the deal and assumed 29.5 percent of the debt. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
